changes.before: Let $S$ be a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ and $x\in S$. The point $x$ is a **smooth point of $S$** if there exist an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $x$, an integer $n\ge0$ and an open subset $V\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ such that $U$ and $V$ are isomorphic as classical varieties over $\mathbb C$; $S$ is **smooth** if every point of $S$ is smooth.
changes.after: Let $S$ be a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ and $x\in S$. The point $x$ is a **smooth point of $S$** if its algebraic local ring $\mathcal O_{S,x}$ is a regular local ring: a nonzero Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ satisfies $\dim_{\mathbb C}(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2)=\dim\mathcal O_{S,x}$ ([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]). The residue field at a classical complex point is $\mathbb C$. The variety $S$ is **smooth** if every point is smooth. This intrinsic algebraic condition does not require a Zariski neighbourhood to be algebraically isomorphic to an open subset of affine space.

changes.before: with the structure sheaf restricted from $X$
changes.after: with its reduced induced algebraic structure (locally the polynomial-quotient function sheaf on the locally closed algebraic set)

changes.before: (ii) Smoothness: the condition is independent of the choices of $U$ and $V$, because a composite of two local isomorphisms to open subsets of affine spaces is again one; no statement about regular local rings, dimension or resolutions is used.
changes.after: (ii) Smoothness is the intrinsic regular-local-ring condition of [[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]] on the algebraic stalk. An isomorphism of classical varieties induces an isomorphism of its local ring, maximal ideal and cotangent space, so the condition is chart-independent. This definition asserts no existence of smooth strata and no analytic-chart comparison theorem. (iii) A locally closed subvariety has its own reduced polynomial-quotient function sheaf; the inverse-image of the ambient structure sheaf is not substituted for that quotient structure.

changes.before: The long exact cohomology sequence of the cone then exhibits each $H^j(C(f))|_S$ as an extension of such local systems, hence again locally constant of finite rank;
changes.after: The long exact cohomology sequence of the cone then exhibits each $H^j(C(f))|_S$ as an extension of such local systems. Such an extension is locally split: around a fixed point trivialize the quotient and kernel, lift the finitely many quotient basis germs along the stalkwise epimorphism, represent those lifts by sections on a common neighbourhood, and shrink until their images equal the constant quotient basis sections. Those lifts define a sheaf section of the epimorphism and hence a direct-sum trivialization of the extension. Thus it is locally constant of finite rank;
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field.

changes.before: The mapping cone of $k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k$ is quasi-isomorphic to $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}$
changes.after: The mapping cone of $k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k$ is quasi-isomorphic to $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}[1]$

changes.before: so the cone triangle is the localization triangle of the derived category
changes.after: so rotating the cone triangle gives $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}[1]$, the localization triangle of the derived category
